mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.10 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.5% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending power and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months where UNRATE exceeds 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales indicate a contraction in consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline by at least 0.5% from the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% year-over-year), a decline in industrial production signals a weakening supply chain that reduces corporate output and profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% YoY and INDPRO declines by at least 0.3% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI inflation rate exceeds 3.5% year-over-year, it triggers a monetary policy tightening expectation that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months where CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly growth rate in real GDP above 2.0% signals strong economic expansion that boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of quarters where GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in unemployment rate and declines in nonfarm payrolls indicate a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate revenue, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE rises by at least 0.2% and PAYEMS declines by at least 0.3% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production falls below 104.0 (index 2017=100) in a month, it signals a contraction in manufacturing output that reduces corporate profits and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months where INDPRO falls below 104.0.
